intro.say: Another face from behind a sealed door. Didn't think Haven 12 was still breathing. Marla Voss. I keep the peace in Dustwell, what there is of it.

opts.t: My shelter's recycler is dead. I need a coolant regulator.

part.say: A regulator. Only place in this valley that ever had parts like that is the Meridian plant. And Meridian is what's killing us. Seems your trouble and mine are the same trouble.

story.say: The reactor woke up two winters back. Nobody knows how. Since then the wells run green and half the town is coughing. Doc Halloran at Bunker Nine swears he can prove where the poison comes from, if somebody brings him samples.

accept.say: Draw a flask from our well, right there in the square. Then one from any of the glowing pools out in the waste. Don't wade in. Take both to Halloran, south-east road. And take these, you'll want them.

consequent.value: I know what you've been doing out there. Keep your hands where I can see them and say your piece.
Good to see you, friend. Dustwell owes you more than it can pay. What do you need?

opts.t: Any word on your missing deputies?
I found your deputies. I'm sorry.

chip.say: That's it. That's the real chip. Dustwell owes you. Take this, it's hide armor off a raider I made regret his life choices.

dir.say: Bunker Nine is south-east along the road. The Relay Tower is far west, Wick lives under it. Meridian is dead north and I wouldn't go without armor. Hound Dens are just north of town. Cass at the saloon knows the rest.

town.say: Sixty-one people, nine goats, one well. We trade scrap for bullets and bullets for food. Before the reactor woke we were nearly comfortable. Now I bury somebody every month.

work.say: Kess's raiders at Gantry Yard took our purifier chip. Get it back any way you can stomach. Past that: the bounty board by my office pays for pests, Duggan wants scrap, Brannock lost his tools, and Cass has hound trouble.

lights.say: Lights. We have lights, and the well gauge is dropping back toward clean. Castellan's people are stringing wire down the main street like it's a festival. You fixed the damned thing. I didn't know that was on the table.

opts.t: Neither did I, until I was standing there.

scram.say: The glow is gone off the north horizon. The wells will clear in a season. ...That part in your pack. Our purifier plant has been dead since before I was born, for want of one. I'd trade every gun in this town for it. But I know who sent you out here.

opts.t: Dustwell needs it more. Take it.

home.say: Then go, and no hard feelings. Tell your Overseer the door works both ways.

lp.say: Hal and Benny. Good boys, too young for it. Rode out to the Hound Dens chasing a stolen goat. Three days, nothing. Find them, {name}. Whatever you find.

lpdone.say: Hal's badge. I gave him that myself. ...Thank you for bringing it back, and for the hounds. I'll tell their mothers it was quick.

vj.say: Rides the western road with four guns and a sack of bird feed he throws on the bodies. Camp somewhere past Rattlesnake Gulch, far west. Bring me the tag he wears in his ear and the bounty is yours.

vjdone.say: That's his tag, sure enough. The western road just got a lot quieter. Three hundred and fifty chits, from me and every caravan master in the valley.

consequent.value: Uh. Cash up front, friend. No offence. Lots of offence, actually.

alternate.value: Chits talk, friend. What can Pocket do for you?

opts.t: How do prices work around here?
Madame Vex wants her three hundred chits.

scrap.say: Eight scrap metal, three circuit boards. Ruins and wrecks are full of both. Bring them and I'll make it worth your while, and I'll open the good shelf for you.

scrapdone.say: Beautiful! Clean, no rust rot. Here's your cut. Have a look at the stock again, I've put the caravan goods out.

prices.say: Every trader pays more for what they deal in: I like junk, Brannock likes iron, the Doc likes medicine. We all restock at sunrise, and none of us has bottomless pockets. Do right by the town and we shave the price. Charm doesn't hurt either.

debt.say: Three hundred? I haven't SEEN three hundred since before the bombs. Please, I've got stock to buy, I've got...

opts.t: Pay up or I start breaking stock.
I'll cover it myself. Pay me back when you can.
Pay her fifty a week. I'll sell her on it.

debtthreat.say: All right! All right. Here. That's the till and my lucky coin. Happy?

debtpaid.say: You... you'd do that? I'll pay you back. Some of it. Most of it. I'll try.

debtdeal.say: Fifty a week? I can do fifty a week. I can almost do fifty a week. Thank you, friend.

consequent.value: tomas

hub.say: Pull up a stool. Drink's warm, company's warmer.

consequent.value: Rent a bed (free).

opts.t: Heard you have a hound problem.
You look like something is eating you.
Saltreach's mayor sent me about the aquifer.
Any work at the Dry Hole?

hounds.say: Mutant hounds north of town, at the old Dens. Five of them at least. Kill five and I'll make it worth your time.

houndsdone.say: You actually did it! Here, take Pop's old scatter gun and some shells.

brother.say: My brother Tomas. He went scavenging at the Collapsed Depot nine days back, with our mother's locket for luck. It's east, off the Bunker road. If you're headed that way... just look. Please.

tomas.say: That's... that's Ma's locket. Where did you get that?

opts.t: He didn't make it, Cass. I'm sorry. He's at the depot.
He sold it to me. Said he was heading east with a caravan.

truth.say: ...I knew. Nine days, I knew. Thank you for not making me keep wondering. I'll bring him home. You eat free here, and the bed's yours whenever you want it.

lie.say: East! That idiot. That beautiful idiot. He always said he'd see the coast. Here, take this, it's what I'd saved to pay a search party.

rumor.say: They say Kess keeps her loot under a very paranoid lock. People in hoods at the Burned Chapel carry lanterns in daylight. Hollis Grange out west lost half his herd to a boar the size of a car. And somebody saw a dog sitting by the Collapsed Depot, just waiting. Oh, and there's a casino on the Gantry road now, the Silver Spur. Lou runs a straight table there, they say.

cr.say: Just one. This goes to Oskar Vane in Saltreach. It's sealed, and it stays sealed. Fifty chits on delivery, and a drink on the house when you're back.

wrc.say: Ines sent you? Fine. Dustwell dug the first wells into that aquifer forty years ago, with our hands. Saltreach just sits on top of it and calls it theirs. We'd share. We just won't be told.

dh.say: I want a house special. Something that glows in the glass. Three clean waters and two glow fungus and I'll do the rest. Mostly safe. Mostly.

dhdone.say: Watch. ...See that? Glows. Doesn't bite, much. First two are on the house. Well, they're yours. Don't drink them both at once.

hub.say: Brannock. If it shoots, I fix it. If it doesn't shoot, I fix that too.

opts.t: What's that buggy behind the shop?
Need anything for that project in the back?

tools.say: Raiders hit my wagon up on the north ridge, east of the reactor road. Took my tool roll. Forty years of files and reamers. Bring it back and I'll put something special in your hand.

toolsdone.say: Every one of them still in its loop. Ha! Here. I built this for myself and never had the nerve to carry it. She's called Promise.

advice.say: Workbench is behind me. Tune a gun three times and it's a different gun, but you'll need gears past the first. Aim down the barrel and stop moving. And a revolver doesn't jam, which is more than I can say for people.

buggy.say: The Rust Runner. Raced her on the salt flats before the war took the salt. Bring me three gears, five scrap and two circuits, and she's yours. I'm too old to drive anything faster than a grudge.

buggydone.say: Give me an hour... There. She coughs, she rattles and she'll do ninety downhill. Key's yours. Try not to hit anyone you like.

bc.say: Cinder Quarry has a storehouse full of blasting powder the raiders don't know how to use. I know how to use it. Bring me a crate and I'll turn some of it into something useful for you.

bcdone.say: Careful, careful... lovely. Three pipe bombs, fresh off the bench, and some chits. Don't throw them indoors.

sd.say: Ten good lumps of scrap and four gears that turn. What for? A surprise. A loud one. Pays well.

sddone.say: Beautiful. Every one of them. Here. And when you hear a very large noise from Dustwell next month, you didn't hear it from me.

hub.say: Don't touch the antenna! ...oh. Hello. I'm Wick. I'm making this old relay talk again.

opts.t: Who sent the reactor a cold-start command?
What have you got on the bench?
Anything you need from out there?
The booster on the overpass is live.

log.say: Cold-start? ...Oh. Oh no. Two winters ago, 03:12. It didn't originate here, I only relayed it. It came up the old highway line from the roadside emergency terminal at the Dry Overpass, east of Gantry. Whoever typed it signed it. Go and read it.

need.say: Three fusion cells. There's one in each of three ruins: the Collapsed Depot, the Burned Chapel, and the Dry Overpass. Bring them to the terminal here and I'll boot it. Then I can sell you things that hum.

status.say: Cells in the terminal over there, please. I'm vibrating.

drones.say: Meridian security drones! Three of them, circling the dish and zapping anything that hums, including me. Their logic cores are worth a lot to me, if you bring any back.

opts.t: I'll knock them out of the sky.

dronesdone.say: The dish is singing again! Here, cells for the trouble, and I'll pay top chits for any logic cores you find.

bb.say: There's one thing. The last relief plane out of Kestrel Airfield came back without its pilot. The flight recorder's still in Hangar 2. I want to hear it. I want to know what she saw up there.

bbdone.say: Let me... there. Static, then her voice. "Kestrel relief, engine two out, I'm putting down on the north flats." Then nothing. Captain Ruth Abara. She didn't come back with the plane because she wasn't in it. She bailed. North flats, past the airfield.

bo.say: With a booster on the overpass mast it can. Two circuits and two lengths of copper, wired into the junction box at the top of the ramp. Then Saltreach can hear us, and we can hear them complain.

bodone.say: There it is. Saltreach on channel nine, loud and clear, already complaining. Here, cells, and my eternal professional respect.

hub.say: Careful, careful. You smell like shelter air. Good. Sterile.

opts.t: I need a way into the core chamber.
I have the two Rad Flush.
Anything I can do for you?
I brought the supplies for the fever cure.

proof.say: Same isotope in both flasks. Meridian No. 2, no question. But look at the decay curve. That plant did not wake up by itself. Somebody woke it: a cold-start command, two winters ago, relayed through Relay 4. Wick logs everything. Go and ask him who.

proof2.say: On purpose, yes. To poison us? I doubt it. Nobody restarts a reactor to kill a well. They wanted the lights back. They just did not know what was broken inside.

spare.say: I keep one spare keycard and I am too frightened to use it. I won't hand it to someone who can't walk back out. Bring me two Rad Flush. Prove you can keep yourself alive in there, and it's yours, no promises asked.

card.say: Here. The chamber is south of the cooling tower. What lives in it used to be Chief Engineer Abbott. He was holding the replacement regulator when the alarms went. He still is.

fungus.say: The fungus that grows at the edge of the glowing pools. It eats radiation and turns it into something that knits tissue. Four clumps of it and I can prove it. Pick them from the edge. The edge!

fungusdone.say: Remarkable. Look at that. Here, the first batch, and I'll write the recipe on your wrist computer: one Stim Shot, one fungus cap, any workbench.

rf.say: Rad fever. Half my people can't stand up. Three Rad Flush and a glow fungus cap and I can brew enough cure for everyone. Fungus is the active ingredient. Don't ask.

rfdone.say: That's everything. Give me an hour and I'll have them on their feet. Take these stims. If you ever get rad fever, come here first.

consequent.value: hub

intro.say: Easy. You've come a long way to stand in a burned church. ...You read the terminal, then. Rosalind Castellan. My grandmother ran Meridian's night shift. I sent the command.

why.say: I gave this valley power. For one winter Dustwell had heat and the children stopped dying of cold. Then the coolant regulator failed and the leak began. The thing that used to be Chief Engineer Abbott killed two of mine before we got the chamber sealed. He still carries the replacement part.

opts.t: So what now? Fix it, or kill it?

plan.say: Kill the core and the wells clear, and we go back to burning furniture. Fit the new regulator and it runs clean for a hundred years. Lights. Pumps. A purifier that works. I have a keycard. What I don't have is someone who can walk past Abbott.

hub.say: The lamp stays lit. What do you need?

opts.t: Give me the keycard. I'll install the regulator. You have my word.
Give me the keycard. I'll decide when I'm standing in front of it.
It's done. The core is running clean.

sworn.say: Then take it. At the control terminal, install the regulator. Do not pull the scram lever. I am trusting you with the only future I've got.

honest.say: ...At least you're honest. Take it. Just look at Dustwell's dark windows on your way north, before you choose.

refuse.say: Then find another way in. Halloran keeps a spare, and he's too frightened to use it himself.

haven.say: Then open your door and come up here, where it's needed. One part can't save a hole in the ground and a whole valley both. I'm sorry. That's the arithmetic.

lamp.say: Engineers' grandchildren, mostly. We kept the manuals when everyone else burned them for warmth. We carry a light in the daytime so nobody forgets what one looks like.

thanks.say: I saw the tower beacon change colour from here. I didn't believe it until the chapel bulb came on. A hundred years, vault-born. You gave them a hundred years.

consequent.value: You gave me your word. ...No. I woke the thing, I don't get to be angry. Go. Leave me the lantern.

alternate.value: I know. I watched the glow go out. Clean water and a dark valley. Perhaps that's the wiser trade. I couldn't have made it.

hub.say: Finch Caravan, finest goods between here and salt water. Prices reflect the scenery.

opts.t: Why are you camped under a bridge?

ledger.say: Because scuttlers hit my camp out west and dragged a satchel off to their nest, far north-west past the tower. My ledger's in it. Every debt from here to the coast. I can't leave without it and I'm not built for bug holes.

ledgerdone.say: Oh, you lovely creature. Take these leathers off my guard's back, he owes me anyway. And from now on you pay what my friends pay.

world.say: More of this, mostly. A town on stilts in the salt flats. A city that still has a mayor. Nobody out there has a working reactor, I'll tell you that. If this valley ever gets its lights on, the caravans will come here. And if you need a rifle that isn't yours, Jory by the wagons hires out.

sv.say: Badly. Nobody goes to the edges. Walk to Cinder Quarry, Kestrel Airfield, the KDST station and Fort Ironside, and tell me what's really there. Honest distances. Honest dangers.

svdone.say: Quarry, airfield, radio station, fort. You actually went. This is the first true map in eighty years, and your name is in the corner. Here, you've earned a surveyor's fee.

consequent.value: You've earned a seat at my fire. Speak.
Heard about you. You're my kind of trouble. Talk.

alternate.value: You've got guts walking into my yard. Talk fast.

opts.t: Who's the one cleaning her rifle by the containers?

chip.say: The chip? Sure. One-fifty chits. Or do a job for me. Or earn it in blood. Your call.

opts.t: Hand it over, or I start breaking things.
A town with clean water buys more of your salvage.

job.say: Rudd's Jackals. They're squatting on MY salvage north-west of here. Paint the sand with them and the chip is yours, plus a seat at my fire and a look at my stores.

yarddone.say: Rudd's dead? Ha! I heard the shooting from here. A deal's a deal. My stores are open to you.

paid.say: Pleasure doing business. You can buy from the stores now, too.

scared.say: ...Take it. Just take it. Keep walking.

smart.say: Huh. Customers who aren't dying. That's almost clever. Take the chip. Tell Voss she owes me a discount.

reg.say: The heart of Meridian, in a backpack. Whoever holds that decides who gets clean water, forever. Twelve hundred chits, right now, and nobody in this valley ever lays a hand on you again.

arguments.value: Sold the valley's water to Kess

sable.say: Sable. Best shot I have and the worst attitude. If she leaves with you, you owe me a rifle. Kidding. Mostly.

intro.say: {name}. Good, you're awake. Don't sit down, there isn't time. You heard the pumps stop in the night.

opts.t: I heard Pell swearing at them since midnight.

recycler.say: The coolant regulator in the water recycler cracked. Pell says it can't be patched again, and there is no spare. We have nine days of clean water. Four hundred people.

plan.say: Before the war, a plant called Meridian Atomics used the same regulator. If one still exists, it is up there. I am opening the door, {name}. I am sending you.

opts.t: I'll go. I'll bring it back.

whyme.say: Because you had the best marks in Security training in forty years. And because you are the only one who ever asked me what the sky looks like. Now you get to find out.

refuse.say: Then four hundred people die of thirst slowly, and you with them. I would rather you went up there with a pistol and my blessing.

orders.say: Draw your gear from the Security locker across the corridor. Pell wants a word before you leave. Then the great door. Once it closes behind you, it stays closed until you come home with that part.

hub.say: Locker, Pell, then the door. Nine days, {name}.

surface.say: Our records say the bombs took everything. They also say the coffee machine was repaired in 2061, so believe what you like. Just come home.

consequent.value: hub

intro.say: Don't touch that, it's holding the other thing together. You're the one going up? Then listen. Coolant regulator, model R-7. Size of a loaf of bread, twice as heavy, Meridian stamp on the housing. Nothing else will fit.

opts.t: Can't you fix the old one?

fix.say: I've fixed it nine times. It isn't a part any more, it's a memory of one. One more crack and the loop floods with silt. Bring me a new one.

tips.say: The surface has weather. I've read about it. Apparently it just happens to you. Keep your water clean and your pistol cleaner. Find a workbench and tune that thing before it tunes you.

gift.say: Here. Tape and scrap. Everything up there is broken, so you'll want to be able to fix things. Good luck.

arguments.value: Received Duct Tape x2, Scrap Metal x3

hub.say: R-7. Meridian stamp. Don't come back with a toaster.

consequent.value: hub

intro.say: There you are, sweet pea. The Overseer told me everything, and I told her she was a fool, and then I packed you a lunch. Two stews and a tin of the meat nobody asks about.

opts.t: Thank you, Nan. I'll come back.

arguments.value: Received Ortiz Stew x2, Canned Mystery Meat
Received Ortiz Stew x2, Canned Mystery Meat

bye.say: You come back to us. And if the sky really is blue up there, you remember it for me.

hurt.say: Pride is heavy, {name}, and you'll be carrying enough up there. Take it anyway.

hub.say: Go on, before I start crying into the soup.

consequent.value: done
The water tastes like water again. Imagine that. Still, an old woman gets hungry. Anything to spare?

alternate.value: Spare some clean water for an old woman? The well's gone sour and my grandson won't stop coughing.

opts.t: Get away from me, old woman.
Is there anything you miss from before Dustwell?

thanks.say: Bless you. There's still people out here, then. Not just guns walking around with legs.

scorn.say: Mm. The wastes make some folk hard. Mind it doesn't make you empty.

done.say: You've done enough today, dear. Come by tomorrow and I'll tell you about the war. I was very young.

tt.say: Thaddeus played the harmonica every night. Badly. I would give anything to hear it again, even badly. We left it in the eastern ruins, in the house with the blue door, when the dogs came.

ttdone.say: Oh... oh, it still smells like him. Tobacco and tin. I can't play a note. I don't care. Take these, child. You gave an old woman back her evenings.

opts.t: Easy, girl. Easy. Nobody's hurting you.

joined.say: The dog eats like it has not in days, then sniffs your hand and gets up beside you. The tag on its collar is stamped BISCUIT.

party.say: Biscuit sits, tail sweeping the dust, waiting for you to decide.

opts.t: Go home to Dustwell. Cass will feed you.

intro.say: Jory Vance. I keep Finch's wagons in one piece. Between jobs, I hire out.

opts.t: What kind of work do you take?

rules.say: Escort, clearing, the occasional stubborn door. What I don't do is shoot people who aren't shooting at us. You start doing that, I walk.

consequent.value: Finch says you got her ledger back. First month's on the house.

alternate.value: A hundred and fifty chits, up front, and I keep what I find on my own kills.

hired.say: Then let's go. I'll take the right side. Try not to walk in front of my rifle.

refuse.say: I've heard what you do out there. Find someone else to hold your coat.

opts.t: We're done here. Go back to Finch.

consequent.value: Honestly? Best job I've had. You make me feel like the good guys still exist.
I'm watching you, boss. Don't give me a reason.

alternate.value: Feet hurt. Rifle's clean. That's a good day out here.

consequent.value: party
refuse

intro.say: Sable. I do the shooting Kess is too lazy to do herself. I am getting very bored of it.

opts.t: Want to come with me instead?

bored.say: Same rust, same faces, same three songs on the same broken radio. You look like you go places. Places have things in them.

consequent.value: Kess likes you, so she won't shoot me in the back for leaving. Probably. I'm in.

alternate.value: Kess won't like it. That's half the appeal. Cover my tab, a hundred chits, and I'm yours.

joined.say: Ha! Finally. Point me at something loud.

refuse.say: You? You'd have me handing out soup. Pass, saint.

opts.t: Why did you really leave Kess?

why.say: Kess sells water. I watched a kid try to pay her in buttons once. She laughed. I didn't. That's all.

consequent.value: I know your face. Keep your hands off my herd and we'll get along.

alternate.value: Hollis Grange. Forty oxen, once. Thirty-one now, and I know who's eating them.

opts.t: Old Tusker is dead. Here are the hides.
Do you have any seeds? Real ones, for Haven 12.
Old Scar is dead. Here's his pelt.

tusker.say: Boar the size of a car. Scarred up like a road map. Comes down from the hills west of the Relay Tower and takes a calf a week. Kill it and bring me three hides as proof, and you'll eat for a month.

paid.say: Ha! That's him, all right. Here, steaks and chits. And you're welcome at my fire any night.

life.say: Oxen don't care about the end of the world. They want grass, water and somebody to stand between them and the teeth. Simple. I like simple.

ru.say: Rustlers took two of my oxen last night. Tracks lead north-west, toward the hills above Haven 12. Three of them, maybe. I want my animals back more than I want them dead, but I'm not fussy.

rudone.say: Both girls walked home on their own this morning, chewing like nothing happened. Here. Steaks from a different ox, don't worry. And chits.

seeds.say: Seeds? Bean, squash, maize, and some tomato from my greenhouse. Here. Tell your vault people to talk to the plants. They like it.

os.say: Old Scar. A stalker the size of a cart horse, ear torn half off. Comes down from the hills north-east of the Hound Dens and takes an ox a week. Kill it and I'll pay what I've got.

osdone.say: Lord, look at the size of it. I'll sleep tonight for the first time in a month. Here, chits, and hides from the boars. You earned every one.

consequent.value: You've had a remarkable evening, darling. The Spur would love to see you again. Tomorrow.
I know exactly what you are, {name}. Spend money here and we'll stay friends.

alternate.value: Welcome to the Silver Spur. Cards, wheel and machines, and the only clean glasses south of the reactor.

opts.t: I found this inside Old Patsy.
I want to play at the high-roller tables.
I've made peace with the Spur. Do I get a VIP marker?
How did you end up running a casino?

story.say: I ran water before I ran cards. Water makes you enemies. Cards make you friends who owe you money. I prefer the second kind.

rules.say: Blackjack pays three to two and the dealer stands on seventeen. The wheel has one green zero. The machines pay what they pay. Win too much and Knuckles walks you to the door, with a smile.

chip.say: Ah. So you're the curious kind. That little chip keeps the lights on, sweetheart. Three hundred chits says you put it back and forget you ever saw it.

opts.t: Deal. Three hundred and I never saw it.
Make the machines honest, publicly, or the whole valley hears about this.

bribed.say: A pleasure doing business. Drinks are on the house tonight. Only the drinks.

honest.say: ...You drive a hard bargain. Fine. The machines go honest and I tell everyone it was my idea. Here, for your trouble, and your silence about the last three years.

vip.say: High-roller chips and the big limits. Five hundred chits for the marker, and you keep it for life. The house likes its whales well fed.

vipfree.say: Since you were so... civilized about Old Patsy. Take it. A gift. Gifts are the house's most profitable investment.

vipyes.say: Welcome to the gold tables, darling. Chips up to five hundred, and the wheel takes two thousand a spin.

pd.say: Pocket Duggan owes the house three hundred chits and keeps sending me apologies instead. Collect it. How is your business.

consequent.value: Paid in full. How very efficient of you.
A payment plan. How... modern. Fine. The house can be patient when it's profitable.

alternate.value: You squeezed it out of him. I don't want to know how. Here's your fee.

consequent.value: Old Patsy paid a jackpot to a widow from Dustwell last night. Whole room cried. I cried. You did that, {name}.

alternate.value: Lucky Lou, at your service. Cards are honest at my table. Can't say the same for every corner of this room.

opts.t: What do you mean, not every corner?
I pulled this out of Old Patsy.
Why do they call you Lucky?
Bet me I can't walk out a big winner?
A thousand up, Lou. Pay up.

patsy.say: Old Patsy. The machine by the bar. Three years, no jackpot. People feed it their water money. Get a look inside her, would you? There's a service panel round the back, if you're good with your hands.

chip.say: A governor. I knew it. Vex will pay you to keep quiet, or you can rip it out and let everybody win fair. Or you could flash that thing for yourself. I won't pretend I didn't think about that.

opts.t: Rip it out. Let people win fair.
I'll flash it so Patsy pays me.

fair.say: Here. A hundred chits from my own tip jar, and I'd pay double. Vex will figure it out, but she can't prove it was you.

mine.say: Huh. Well. Just don't empty her in one night, or Knuckles will notice. I never saw a thing.

lucky.say: Walked out of the Meridian blast zone with all my fingers. Been gambling on borrowed time ever since. Seems a shame to stop now.

tips.say: Blackjack, stand on twelve when I show a six or less. Never take insurance. On the dice, the pass line is the friendliest bet in the house. And the wheel? The wheel is for people who like watching their money spin before it leaves.

hr.say: Ha! Alright. Walk out of here a thousand chits ahead in one night and I'll pay you two-fifty out of my own pocket. Lose, and you buy the next round for the whole room.

hrdone.say: A thousand up. You lucky so-and-so. Two-fifty, as promised. Now get out before Vex notices you exist.

consequent.value: House says you're done for tonight. No hard feelings.
I'm watching you. Weapons stay holstered in here.

alternate.value: Evening. Keep your gun in its holster and your hands off the dealer.

night.say: Two fights, one proposal, a guy who tried to pay with a pre-war toaster. Toaster worked, though.

consequent.value: thanks

hub.say: Thank the sky. My water ran out two days ago and my leg's bad. Can you spare anything?

opts.t: Here, a stimpak for the leg.

gave.say: Bless you. Here, it isn't much, but I found this out on the flats. Better in your hands.

robbed.say: Take it. Take it all. I hope it's heavy.

thanks.say: I'll make it to Dustwell now. I won't forget your face.

hub.say: Easy, easy. Just a trader and her ox-less cart. Prices are fair-ish and the company's free.

elements.value: Vultures thick over the Hound Dens today. Something died big.
There's a casino out on the Gantry road now. The Silver Spur. Everyone loses, but they lose in style.
Brannock's been tinkering with some engine behind his shop. Loud.
Radstorm out west yesterday. Green sky, Geiger going like hail. Get indoors if you see one.

consequent.value: Knuckles says you cleaned us out tonight. Have one on the house on your way out, then scram.
I pour for anybody, but I count the glasses after you.

alternate.value: What'll it be, {name}? The sour's my own recipe. Lou swears it makes the cards fall kind.

opts.t: How long have you worked the Spur?
What's in the Lucky Sour, really?

elements.value: The fella at the dice table rolled eleven passes in a row last week. Vex had him searched. Clean. Some folks just have it.
Knuckles used to fight in the pits at Gantry. Lost one fight in nine years, and he still won't say who to.
Madame Vex keeps a ledger of who owes her. Half of Dustwell is in it. Pocket's in it twice.
Somebody's been selling fake Spur markers in Dustwell. Real ones ring when you drop them. Fakes go thunk.

history.say: Six years. I poured at the Dry Hole in Dustwell before that. Vex offered me double and a door that locks. In this valley a door that locks is worth more than double.

sour.say: Cactus juice, lime from Hollis's greenhouse, a splash of something Brannock distills, and a pinch of salt for the tears of the house. Mostly it's the salt.

consequent.value: Saltreach doesn't turn anyone away, {name}. But we do keep count of who's inside the walls.

alternate.value: Welcome to Saltreach. Salt, water and a roof, in that order. What can the town do for you?

opts.t: What do you know about Haven 12?
I can deal with your wagon raiders.
You mentioned the aquifer. What's the dispute?
I've heard Dustwell's side. Let's settle the water.
What can be done about Mother Rust?
Mother Rust is dead. Here's her crown.
A raider called Renn wants to start over here. I'll vouch for him.

town.say: We pan salt from the flats, cure meat with it and trade it to every town between here and the reactor. Salt keeps. Salt doesn't rot. In a valley like this, that makes it money.

who.say: I do, until somebody better wants the job. Oskar runs the salt. Jun keeps the engines alive. Mother Hale keeps everyone fed, and Brother Amos keeps everyone honest, mostly.

trouble.say: Raiders out of Rattlesnake Gulch hit our salt wagons twice this month. And Fort Ironside is getting bolder. Mother Rust sends riders to "collect taxes". We haven't had a sheriff since the last one went to talk to her.

haven.say: The vault folk? We traded with them before the door shut for good. Polite people. Paid in water chits and never once looked us in the eye.

sw.say: Bless you. They hole up in Rattlesnake Gulch, west past Dustwell, in a ring of rocks like a nest. Five guns, maybe more. Clear them out and the salt flows again.

swdone.say: The wagons came back whole this morning. Every one. Here, from the town chest. Saltreach remembers its friends.

wr.say: The deep aquifer runs under the flats and under Dustwell both. They say it's theirs because their wells were first. We say it's ours because the water rises here. Talk to Cass at the Dry Hole, she speaks for Dustwell. Then come back and help me find a deal that doesn't end in shooting.

opts.t: Split it by need: measured shares, a joint well crew, no tolls.
Saltreach keeps the aquifer. Dustwell pays a toll.
Dustwell was there first. Their claim stands.

wrfair.say: Measured shares and a joint crew. Cass will grumble and then agree, because it's fair. You'd make a fine mayor, {name}. Don't tell anyone I said so.

wrsalt.say: Well. Saltreach will be rich, and Dustwell will remember who made it so. Here's your share. Spend it far from Dustwell.

wrdust.say: Honest, if not profitable. I'll draft the letter. We'll pan our salt and buy our water like everyone else. Thank you for not lying to me.

sh.say: Somebody brave, honest and not a raider. Or somebody brave and honest who used to be a raider, I'm not fussy. I heard the vault folk train their security officers properly.

consequent.value: Renn, is it? A deserter for a deputy. Saltreach has done stranger things. The badge is his, and the reward is yours.

alternate.value: An officer from Haven 12! Discipline and good boots. Dunn arrives next week. Thank you, {name}.

ic.say: Kill her, and Ironside falls apart in a week. Her lieutenants hate each other more than they hate us. Bring me her crown and I'll know it's done. Fort Ironside is far north-west, past the Relay Tower. Bring friends.

icdone.say: The Iron Crown. I'll hang it in the town hall where every raider can see it. Four hundred chits, and Saltreach owes you more than chits.

renn.say: A Gulch raider. In my town. You're sure?

opts.t: He walked away from them. That counts for something.
He'll work off his debt guarding the salt wagons.

rennyes.say: Fine. He sleeps in the guardhouse and draws no weapon inside the square for a month. If he turns, it's on both of you.

hub.say: Vane Salt Company. Finest crust on the flats, if you can chew it. Buying or browsing?

opts.t: How do you get salt out of a desert?
Teodor is safe. He's on his way home.

salt.say: Flood a pan with brine from the deep well, let the sun take the water, rake what's left. Slow, honest work. My brother Teodor did the raking. Before.

worried.say: Teodor went to Cinder Quarry three weeks ago to buy blasting powder. He hasn't come back. The quarry's crawling with raiders now. I'm not a brave man, {name}. I just sell salt.

lbyes.say: You would? He went to Cinder Quarry, south past Haven 12. The raiders there keep anyone useful. Teodor is very useful. He can smell a salt vein through solid rock.

lbdone.say: He's... he walked in an hour ago, thin as a rake and grinning. Take this. Take more if you need it. Anything from the shop, a fair price, forever.

parcel.say: Ah. Cass's "parcel". Thank you. You didn't open it, I hope?

opts.t: I opened it. Torn ledger pages from the town hall, Oskar.

parcelok.say: Good. Cass and I have an... arrangement about water shares. Nothing for you to worry about. Here, for the walk.

parcelcaught.say: ...Keep your voice down. Fine. Yes. Cass and I skimmed the water ledger. Everybody does. What do you want?

opts.t: Give the pages back to the Mayor yourself and pay back what you took.
Two hundred chits and I forget I can read.

parcelhonest.say: You're a hard one. Fine. I'll walk them over myself. Maybe Ines will be merciful. She usually is, which is why we got away with it.

parcelbribe.say: Two hundred. There. Now we're both thieves. Welcome to the salt business.

consequent.value: Is that Brannock's old buggy I heard rattling in? Bring it by if the axle starts singing.

alternate.value: Takeda Garage. If it has an engine, I can make it cough. If it has two, I can make it argue.

opts.t: What have you got for sale?
Where do you get parts out here?
Those airfield drones. Want them gone?

work.say: A water pump for the deep well. It needs a fuel injector, and the only ones left in the valley are at Kestrel Airfield. Which is full of security drones that never got the memo the war ended.

parts.say: Wrecks, mostly. The airfield, the overpass, the old depot. Sometimes Finch's caravan has something good if you catch it on the right day.

inj.say: Hangar 2, at Kestrel Airfield in the north-east. There's a cargo plane inside with its engine cowling off. The injector's a brass cylinder about the size of your forearm. Mind the drones.

injdone.say: Oh, she's beautiful. The pump will run by tonight. Take the Homestead off my wall, and some shells. You've earned a real gun.

gr.say: Four of them, old security drones running on a patrol loop older than both of us. Knock them down and the airfield is open for salvage. I'll pay in energy cells.

consequent.value: Your road has been kind to others, {name}. It shows. Sit, if you like.
Every road can turn. Even yours. The door is always open.

alternate.value: Peace on your road, traveller. The Chapel of the Long Road keeps no gods, only lamps.

opts.t: Why no bell in the tower?
The bell is rigged for hauling at Lakeview Plaza.

faith.say: That everyone is on a long road, that nobody walks it alone, and that a lamp in the window costs very little and means a great deal.

bell.say: Raiders took it. Hauled it off to sell for scrap, then couldn't lift it into a wagon and left it in the old Lakeview Plaza. I'm told it still sits there, under the husks.

cb.say: Lakeview Plaza, west of the Relay Tower. A great dead shopping hall full of husks. Find the bell and rig it with rope; the salt guards will fetch it with a wagon.

cbdone.say: Then tonight, for the first time in two years, Saltreach will hear its bell. Thank you. Every lamp in this chapel will burn for you.

sc.say: My brothers are buried under the Burned Chapel, south-west of Dustwell. Husks have crawled down among them. I cannot bear to think of it. Will you clear them out?

scdone.say: Then they rest. Thank you. I will say their names tonight, and yours after them.

hub.say: Brine & Barrel. Hot stew, cold water, and the beds are only lumpy on one side. What'll it be?

elements.value: A woman came through last week asking for a radio. Wouldn't say why. Paid in pre-war coins.
There's a broadcast at midnight on a dead frequency. Just numbers. Lark at Pilgrim's Rest swears it's a woman counting.
Mother Rust was a cook, you know. Before Ironside. Made a beautiful stew. Now she makes widows.
Jun's been asking about fuel injectors for months. That boy will drive into the airfield one of these days and not come back.

it.say: A week's takings, gone out of a locked box. No broken lock, no broken window. Somebody with a key, or somebody nobody watches. Ask Pip. That child sees everything.

consequent.value: The salt guard? With my own money in his boots? Well. He'll pay it back by washing every pot I own. Here, the finder's share.

alternate.value: You found the thief but not the money? Funny, that. Well, at least I know who to watch.

hub.say: Are you a raider? You don't look like a raider. Raiders have more spikes. Do you have any spikes?

opts.t: What do you do around here?
Did you see anyone near the inn strongbox?
Why do you look so sad, Pip?
Rusty is safe. He's on his way home.

nospikes.say: Good. Mayor says if a raider comes I have to hide in the salt pile. It gets in your ears. It gets everywhere.

job.say: I count wagons. Fourteen this week. Two came back with holes in. Mister Oskar gives me a chit for every ten I count, so I count really carefully.

clue.say: The salt guard went in the back door at night. With a key! Then he bought new boots. Nobody buys new boots. Boots come from dead people.

ru.say: Rusty chased a lizard down the south road and he didn't come back and it's getting dark soon. He has a collar with his name. I made it.

rudone.say: RUSTY! He's here! He's licking my face! You're my best friend now. You can have my Sun Pops. All of them. Okay three.

hub.say: Keep your weapons holstered inside the square. We don't have a sheriff, but we do have a lot of rifles.

opts.t: Nice boots. Paid for with Mother Hale's takings?

accuse.say: ...Keep it down. Look, she charges us double for stew. I took a little back. Here, take some and we'll call it square.

opts.t: All of it goes back to Mother Hale.
Half for me and I saw nothing.

caught.say: Fine. Fine! Here. Don't tell the Mayor. Please.

cut.say: Pleasure doing business. Hale's stew still tastes like a boot either way.

hub.say: Pilgrim's Rest takes in anyone who walks out of the waste. Are you hurt, traveller, or just tired?

opts.t: Do you need help with anything?
Is someone shooting at the pilgrims?
The sniper on the ridge is dead.

pilgrims.say: People walking to the sea. Nobody's sure it's still there. They stop here to rest, and some of them never leave. That's allowed too.

graves.say: Travellers who didn't make it, mostly. Old Tobias digs, I say the words. One plot's empty and waiting: a pilot from the airfield who crashed in the first days. We never found him.

rm.say: A fever is going through the pilgrims. I can make a tonic, but I need three glow fungus from the reactor flats and two bundles of desert herbs. They grow in the gullies around here.

rmdone.say: Perfect. Glow fungus to burn out the fever, herbs to settle the stomach after. Take these, from our own stores. You've saved lives today, and not by shooting anything.

wt.say: Three shots this week, from the ridge to the east. One pilgrim hit in the leg. Whoever it is shoots for sport. Please make it stop.

wtdone.say: Thank you. The pilgrims will walk on tomorrow. I'll tell them a stranger made the road safe. They'll want to know your name, and I'll tell them that too.

hub.say: Mind the fresh ones. They're still settling.

opts.t: How long have you been the gravedigger?
Tell me about the empty grave.
I could look for Captain Abara.
I found her. These were her tags.

long.say: Since my back was straight. Forty years. I've buried better men than me and a few worse. The worse ones dig easier. Lighter conscience.

empty.say: Captain Ruth Abara. Flew relief out of Kestrel the week the bombs fell. Went down somewhere north. If anyone ever finds her tags, I'd like to finish that hole proper.

lf.say: Would you now. The wreck's somewhere on the northern flats, beyond the airfield, they say. Nobody's looked in forty years. Bring me something of hers and I'll close that grave.

lfdone.say: Ruth Abara. Kestrel Relief Wing. Forty years waiting for a name on a stone. I'll cut it this afternoon. You stand there and watch me do it, mind. It matters that someone watches.

hub.say: Oh! A new face. I'm Lark. I'm walking to the sea. Well, I was. I'm resting. For a year so far.

opts.t: Heard anything strange on the radio?
Maybe I can find you a picture of the sea.
I found this. It's the sea.
KDST is back on the air.

sea.say: My mother said it was so big you couldn't see the other side. I'd like to see something too big to see the other side of.

radio.say: Every midnight, on the dead band past KDST. A woman counting. Seven, four, nine, nine. Then static. It gives me shivers. Good ones, I think.

ls.say: Would you? Anything. A painting. A photograph. A drawing on a napkin. I just want to see how blue it is.

lsdone.say: Oh. Oh, look at it. It just keeps going. Thank you. I think I can stay here a while longer now. It's not going anywhere. Neither am I.

da.say: Then we'd have music again! And news, and Mother Hale reading recipes. The station's on the northern ridge. The transmitter needs circuits and copper wire, I think. Lots of wire.

cw.say: Then you heard her too, didn't you? The counting woman. Seven, four, nine, nine. Last night she said something new: "for the chapel that burned". The old chapel west of Dustwell burned years ago...

consequent.value: after

hub.say: Ah, {name}. You were always the one staring out of the window that wasn't there. Off somewhere important?

opts.t: What are the children learning today?

over.say: Then go. And remember what I taught you: measure twice, trust once, and never drink anything that glows.

lesson.say: Arithmetic, water rationing, and the history of the surface. The official version. I keep the unofficial version in a drawer.

after.say: You came back. The children talk about nothing else. Tell me, is the sky really that big?

hub.say: Haven 12 clinic. If you're bleeding, sit. If you're not, I'm very busy pretending to be.

opts.t: You think the reactor logged what happened?

health.say: Fine, except for the water. Every percent the recycler loses, I see it a week later. Kidneys first. Then tempers.

advice.say: Radiation is patient and you are not. Carry Lead Tabs, don't drink from puddles that hum, and if a dog has two heads, believe the other dog.

ml.say: Every shift wrote its log by hand: pressures, temperatures, who was on duty. If someone kept writing that last night, we would finally know whether Meridian failed, or was failed. The control rooms are near the core.

mldone.say: "Coolant pumps 2 and 3 cut by remote command. Not us. Not us." They knew. Somebody sent that order from outside. Thank you. History is a terrible gift, but it is a gift. Take this, for the road.

hub.say: Careful with the tomatoes. They've had a hard year. Haven't we all.

opts.t: How does anything grow down here?
I could find you seeds from the surface.

grow.say: Grow lights, recycled water and a lot of shouting. The lights are pre-war. When the last bulb goes, we eat moss. Find me seeds up there, would you? Real ones.

vs.say: Would you? Real seeds, with the life still in them. Our strains are forty years tired. Ranchers keep seed stock, if there are any ranchers left.

vsdone.say: Beans. Squash. Real maize! Oh, the children are going to eat something green that isn't algae. Haven 12 owes you twice now.

consequent.value: Gear's signed out to you. Try to bring it back with all the same holes.

alternate.value: The locker's at the back. Overseer cleared you, so take what's inside.

opts.t: Saltreach needs a sheriff. You're trained for it.

surf.say: Once, on the last water run. Twenty years ago. Saw a bird. It looked at me like I owed it money.

dunn.say: Me? Leave Haven 12? I... I've been guarding a locker for twenty years. Is it a real town? With real problems?

opts.t: Real problems, real people, and a real sky. They need you more than this locker does.

dunnyes.say: A real sky. All right. I'll pack tonight. Tell the Mayor I'm slow, but I'm thorough.

hub.say: Today's special is algae loaf. Yesterday's special was also algae loaf. I believe in consistency.

opts.t: I could bring you a steak from the surface.

meat.say: Bring me a steak from the surface and I will cook it so well the Overseer will weep. Then I will eat it in front of her.

rm.say: A steak. An actual steak. Bring me one and I will make the Overseer cry, and then I will make you a stew so good you will forget the surface exists.

rmdone.say: Look at the marbling. LOOK at it. I am going to cry first, actually. Here, stew. Three bowls. Come back for the steak dinner; I am inviting the whole vault.

hub.say: The one who cut me loose! Sit, sit. Oskar keeps trying to feed me. I keep letting him.

story.say: I went for powder, they took me for a pickaxe. Six weeks digging their gravel. The worst part was the food. The second worst part was the raiders.

dv.say: Shaft 3, at the quarry. Pure rock salt, a whole wall of it, but scuttlers nested in there before the raiders came. Clear them out, and the Vane Salt Company buys the claim. You get a cut.

dvdone.say: Clear? Ha! Oskar's going to be insufferable. Here's your cut, in advance, before he counts it.

hub.say: Easy! Easy. I'm not with them anymore. I left the Gulch three nights ago and I've been living on lizards since.

why.say: They hit a salt wagon with a kid riding on top. I didn't sign up for that. I signed up for... I don't know what I signed up for. Not that.

where.say: Saltreach, if they'd have me. Somebody would have to vouch, though. Nobody believes a raider.

hub.say: Deputy Renn, Saltreach watch. Still feels strange saying it. Good strange.
Tin Row. Forty-one souls, nine stills, one mayor. That's me. You look like you can count, which already makes you useful.

opts.t: The Toll King is dead. Here's his ledger.

place.say: A car park, once. The cars are walls now and the walls are houses. Every sheet of tin out here has been somebody's roof three times over. We trade, we distil, we don't ask where you're from.

kings.say: Raiders who live under Interstate 9 like trolls under a bridge. The King charges a toll to cross the old highway: water, food, sometimes a person. He calls it "maintenance".

take.say: West of the Hound Dens the interstate crosses the valley. They're under it. Kill the King and bring me his ledger; I want to know who he was paid by.

done.say: "MARKED." He had names ticked. Mine. Sal's. A child's. ...Thank you. Take these, and the rifle from our armory. Tin Row won't forget it.

hub.say: Sal's Scrap! If it rattles, I buy it. If it shoots, I sell it. If it explodes, I sell it at a premium.

opts.t: Where does all this junk come from?

junk.say: The interstate. Thousands of cars stuck on it the night of the sirens. People walked away and never came back. Two hundred years of picking and I'm still finding hubcaps.

hub.say: Welcome to the Tin Cup. Rotgut, water, stew. The rotgut is the cheapest and the stew is the safest, so I always tell people to start in the middle.

news.say: Drones out by the airfield picking the wrecks clean. Pyros with the Kings, the ones who throw fire. And something big with a stinger has been digging under the reactor fence. Pick your road.

hub.say: Sit down, sit down. My knees can't stand up for the both of us. You want a story? I've only got the one, but it's a long one.

war.say: My grandmother called it the Two-Hour War. Two hours of sirens, she said, and then two hundred years of quiet. Nobody here knows who fired first. The radio said it was them; their radio surely said it was us.

road.say: Interstate 9 northbound was the evacuation route. Every car in the valley got on it at once. The patrol closed the bridge at the river to keep the shelters from being overrun. The cars just... stayed. Then the overpass came down at the Dry Wash.

vaults.say: Haven Shelter Company. Sold places in the vaults by subscription, monthly instalments. My family was two payments behind. That's why I'm a story-teller in a tin town and you're a vault dweller with good teeth.

tapes.say: The patrol recorded everything that night on holotapes. They're out there along the interstate, in the cars, by the pillars. Bring me three and I'll finally know if my grandmother made it up.

tapesdone.say: ...That's her voice. "Car four-four-one, lane closed, I have children with me." She didn't make it up. She just left out the part where they turned her away. Thank you, child. Thank you.

hub.say: Are you from a VAULT? Is it true you have a machine that makes snow? Mayor Rook says I ask too many questions. Is that true?

v.say: I KNEW it. When I grow up I'm going to dig my own vault and it's going to have a snow machine and a dog machine and nobody's allowed in unless they're nice.

hub.say: Keep your hands where I can see them and your feet on the right side of the gate. That's the whole of the law in Tin Row.

t.say: Pyros came by with a jerry can last week. I put one down, the rest ran. They'll be back. They always come back, the stupid ones.

hub.say: Morning. Or evening. Hard to tell with the dust.

more.say: Water's been better since the wells cleared. Some of them. If you see a caravan heading east, tell them Ada's still waiting.

hub.say: If you see a caravan heading east, tell them Ada's still waiting.

more.say: Don't go under the interstate after dark. Things live up in the pillars. My father walked here from the coast. Took him two years. He said it was worth it. He was lying.

hub.say: My father walked here from the coast. Took him two years. He said it was worth it. He was lying.

more.say: You can sleep at the Tin Cup if you pay Ezra. You can sleep in the street if you don't mind Bram. Heard the vault folk are out. Heard they're soft. You don't look soft.

hub.say: Heard the vault folk are out. Heard they're soft. You don't look soft.

more.say: Drones took my cousin's cart apart for the copper. With my cousin still on it. The glow in the hills is getting brighter. My goats won't go near it. Smart goats.

hub.say: The glow in the hills is getting brighter. My goats won't go near it. Smart goats.

more.say: I trade jerky for stories. You got a story? No? Then I've got jerky, at full price. Rook's a good mayor. Hard, but good. The good ones are always hard out here.

hub.say: Rook's a good mayor. Hard, but good. The good ones are always hard out here.

more.say: Somebody painted "REMEMBER" on the pillars under the highway. Nobody knows who. Nobody knows what. Morning. Or evening. Hard to tell with the dust.

hub.say: Shhh. Listen. ...Did you hear that? That was the floor. The floor is THIN here, friend. Two doses and you're through it.

opts.t: I brought you a pebble from the Hole.

where.say: The Lattice. Purple grass. Animals made of other animals. A man who rows a boat across nothing. You only get two minutes, and then it spits you out. Sometimes where you went in. Sometimes NOT.

saint.say: I stuck to things. Walls, ceilings, a dog once. The dog was very understanding. People started bringing me offerings. I'm not a real saint. I'm a velcro saint.

take.say: Two doses, back to back, while the first is still singing. Find the three-headed Committee and answer their question. They give pebbles to people who answer right. Bring me one and I'll believe in me again.

done.say: It's WARM. It remembers me. ...I've never been. I just talk. Thank you for going where I only talk about. Take these, and never take them all at once. Or do. I'm not your mother.

hub.say: Welcome welcome WELCOME to the apothecary, I am the doctor, the doctor is me, I have a degree, the degree is a dog's collar but the dog was very smart.

what.say: Horse tranquilliser from a vet clinic, cut with reactor glow and a little bit of love. Mostly glow. One dose, you're a cloud. Two doses, you're the sky's idea of a cloud. Do NOT take three. Nobody knows what three is.

take.say: Three glow caps, two Rad Flush to keep it honest, and a circuit for the stirring machine. The stirring machine is a fan. The fan is a circuit. Hurry, the Feast of Nothing is in, ah, eventually.

done.say: BEAUTIFUL. Look how it glows! It's looking at me! Here, have five, have two fizzy ones, have my undying gratitude, have a nice day, have a hat. No, I need the hat.

hub.say: Please hang your coat on me. I am a coat rack. I have always been a coat rack. ...I am a coat rack missing his hats.

opts.t: You're a man, not a coat rack.

man.say: That is exactly what a coat rack would want you to think, and I am a coat rack, so I would know.

take.say: A bowler, a sunhat and a helmet. The wind took them. The wind is a thief. One is by the cookhouse, one is up the hill on the old sign, one is with the chairs that watch the television that isn't on.

done.say: Bowler. Sunhat. Helmet. ...I am complete. I am a FULL coat rack. Take this coat. It was hanging on me. Everything is hanging on me. That's how I know who I am.

hub.say: Oh, hello. I'm dead, you know. Three days now. I'm only visiting. Don't touch me, you'll go right through. ...Ow. See? Right through.

opts.t: I found your "body". It's a mannequin.

alive.say: That is what the living always say. Rude. Very rude. I was a schoolteacher. Now I'm a ghost who is also, for tax purposes, a schoolteacher.

take.say: Up in the hills east of the Hollow. I took two doses and lay down and when I got up, my body stayed lying there. Go and look. Bring back my locket. I'd like to be buried with it, eventually, whenever I get round to it.

done.say: A MANNEQUIN? Wearing my scarf? ...So that wasn't me lying there. So I'm not dead. So I'm... just here. Oh. Oh, that's much worse. I have to do my laundry. Thank you. I think.

hub.say: Is it Tuesday? Is it? Are you sure? How sure? Did you check? Who checks? Do you know what time it is? Is it later than that?

opts.t: What day do you think it is?

day.say: Do you know I've been asking since the war? Don't you think someone would have answered by now? Isn't that suspicious? Aren't you suspicious? Why aren't you suspicious?

hub.say: *whistles a long, descending note, then two short ones*

p.say: *whistles something that is unmistakably the shape of a question, then points at Mister Pockets, who nods gravely*

hub.say: The reactor. You seen it? Big white boat. Gravy boat. Biggest gravy boat in the world, and nobody's using it. Criminal.

c.say: That's what they WANT you to think. Know what cools? Gravy. Gravy cools. I rest my case. My case is also full of gravy.

hub.say: Ollom vesh, krr-tikka-voon. Ollom VESH. [You are early. You are always early.] Zhaa ne poruul, echo, echo, echo. [Bring me the three that echo.]

take.say: Vrenn. Vrenn ollo. [They float where the ground forgets.] Ti-ti-ti. [Quickly. The door is already closing.]

where.say: Lattice. Laaaa-tisss. [Between your thoughts. Very small here. You are very big. Please mind the furniture.]

done.say: Mmmmmmmm. [The choir is whole.] Kesh. Kesh ollom. [Take the not-key. Now the door waits for you, and brings you home.]

wrong.say: ALL HEADS: Hnnnnn. [Incorrect. Very physical answer. Try again when you are less solid.]

hub.say: Mmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmm. [I am the sound a fridge makes in an empty house. I raised all of the quiet.]

w.say: Mmmm-mm. [Everybody who takes too much comes here for a little while. Most of them only see the colours. You are seeing ME. That is rarer. Do not tell the Committee.]

h.say: MMMMmmmm! [Oh. Oh, that was lovely. Nobody hums back. Your pitch is terrible. Come again.]

idle: Quiet out here. I don't like quiet.
Finch would charge you double for this view.
You ever sleep? Asking for me.
barks.leave: I told you. I don't work for butchers. We're done.

You ever think about just taking things?
Walking is boring. Shooting is not.
barks.leave: You've gone soft, saint. Find another trigger.

lamplight.t: The Meridian core hums the way it was built to. In Dustwell they string bulbs between the rooftops and leave them burning all night, because they can.

sealed.t: The regulator slides home and Haven 12's recycler coughs, shudders and runs. Behind the steel door, four hundred people drink clean water and tell each other the surface is still gone.

dustwell.t: Dustwell's purifier plant turns over for the first time in living memory. Nobody in town remembers what untreated water tastes like by the end of the year.

warlord.t: Kess bolts the regulator into a pump of her own and sells water by the cup. The valley survives. It pays for the privilege.

epilogue.t: Haven 12 could not be saved by a part that was no longer for sale. When the taps ran dry the Overseer opened the door a second time, and the shelter walked north toward the lights.
Ro Castellan never said thank you. She put a lantern on the chapel wall with your number stencilled under it.
The wells cleared within a season. Dustwell stayed dark, and stayed alive. Nobody from Haven 12 came out to see it.
A month later the Haven door opened and stayed open. Dustwell had to build forty new houses, and found it did not mind.
The Lamplighters put out their lanterns and went east. Ro Castellan was last seen walking toward the salt flats, carrying a manual nobody else could read.
Relay 4 kept broadcasting. Three settlements answered in the first week. One of them asked, very politely, who was in charge. Wick said nobody, and meant it as a compliment.
Gantry Yard fell quiet after Kess died. Dustwell's children play on the containers now.
Kess kept her yard and, to everyone's surprise, her word. Her people trade at the Dustwell gate with their weapons slung.
Cass buried her brother on the ridge above town. There is a stool at the end of her bar that nobody else is allowed to use.
Cass still watches the east road at sunset. Some lies are a kindness. This one may not have been.
Brannock took on two apprentices. Every gun that leaves his shop has a small P stamped under the grip.
Halloran's fungal stims went out with the caravans. He named the compound after a patient he could not save.

Across the valley they tell stories about a stranger from under the ground who gave away their own water and never once raised a gun first. Children play at being you. You are remembered as the Lamplight Saint.
People in Dustwell still leave a door open for you. You were not perfect, but when it counted you were kind, and the wasteland does not forget that.
The valley never quite decided what to make of you. You did what the day asked and moved on, the way the dust does.
Mothers in Dustwell bar their doors when your shadow crosses the square. You got what you came for, and the valley remembers the price you made other people pay.

Your name became a word the caravans use to frighten each other at night. Whatever you were when you left that shelter, the wasteland made you into something it fears. You are remembered as the Devil of the Waste.
Back in Haven 12, Nan Okafor kept a bowl of stew warm on the back of the stove every night for a year, just in case.
Biscuit stayed at your side to the end of your days in the valley, and slept across your doorway every night as if something might still come for you.
Jory Vance went back to guarding caravans, and told anyone who would listen that the best job of a long life was walking beside you.
Sable never went back to Gantry Yard. Some say she runs her own caravan now. Some say she robs them. Possibly both.
Grange Ranch grew back to forty head within two years. Hollis named the first calf after you, which was either an honour or a joke.
The Silver Spur became the only honest casino in the valley, mostly because Lucky Lou checked the machines every morning with a screwdriver and a grudge.
Old Patsy kept eating water money for years. Madame Vex sent you a bottle of real whisky every winter, and never a note.
The Rust Runner ended its days on blocks outside Brannock's shop, and kids paid a chit to sit in it and make engine noises.
Fort Ironside fell apart within a month of Mother Rust's death. Her crown still hangs in Saltreach's town hall, and children dare each other to touch it.
The joint well crew of Dustwell and Saltreach became the first thing the two towns ever did together. It was not the last.
Saltreach grew rich on Dustwell's thirst. The toll gate on the aquifer road was burned twice and rebuilt three times.
Captain Ruth Abara has a stone at Pilgrim's Rest now. Pilgrims leave paper planes on it.
KDST played every night after that. Nobody ever found out who the counting woman was, and nobody really wanted to.
People in the valley still lower their voices when they say your name. Not out of respect.
The wasteland is still out there, and it is yours to walk.

> SIGNAL ACQUIRED

...is this thing on? It's on! This is KDST, ten-sixty on your dial, and after nine years of dead air, the valley has a voice again.

Weather: hot. Tomorrow: hot. Saltreach reports the salt wagons running on time. Dustwell says the Dry Hole has a new barrel and it's "only slightly poisonous".

And to whoever climbed up here and fixed this old tower: thank you. Somebody out there is listening tonight because of you.
